locations.name: Iron Ore
locations.summary: Odisha ranks #1 in India in iron ore production. First discovered in Mayurbhanj in 1904.

details.characteristics: Ore varies from magnetite to haematite.
details.notes: First Indian iron ore discovery was at Mayurbhanj in 1904.

locations.name: Manganese Ore
locations.summary: About 30% of India's manganese output — second nationally. The Bonai-Keonjhar belt alone produces ~90% of the state's total.

locations.name: Chromite
locations.summary: Largest chromite producer in India. The Sukinda-Boula-Nuasahi field holds 90% of India's reserves.

keyDeposits: Sukinda-Boula-Nuasahi field, Jajpur (90% of India's reserves)
details.uses: Exported mainly to the USA and Japan.

locations.name: Nickel Ore
locations.summary: Largest nickel producer in India. Found alongside chromite at Sukinda, and in Similipal.

locations.name: Magnetite
locations.summary: Vanadiferrous and titaniferous magnetite deposits in five main belts across Mayurbhanj.

locations.name: Gold
locations.summary: Alluvial deposits in the river valleys and flood plains of the Subarnarekha, Brahmani, and Baitarani.

details.characteristics: Alluvial — recovered from river gravels and flood plains.

locations.name: Platinum Ore
locations.summary: Bhuban-Baripada region holds the world's highest recorded natural platinum values — 220–520 g/tonne.

details.characteristics: 220–520 g/tonne — the highest recorded natural values in the world.

locations.name: Base Metals (Copper, Lead)
locations.summary: Copper and lead deposits, primarily in the Sargipali belt of Sundargarh.

locations.name: Tin Ore
locations.summary: Primary tin production from Malkangiri district.

locations.name: Bauxite
locations.summary: Largest bauxite reserves in India. Occurs as laterite cappings on hill plateaus.

locations.name: Coal
locations.summary: Second largest coal producer in India. Talcher (Brahmani Valley) powers thermal stations; Ib Valley holds 21,000+ million tonnes of reserves.

locations.name: Limestone & Dolomite
locations.summary: Sundargarh alone accounts for ~50% of India's total limestone production. Biramitrapur is a principal source of flux-grade minerals.

details.uses: Flux for steel-making; cement; building stone.

locations.name: Graphite
locations.summary: Found in four main regions of the Eastern Ghats. Carbon content varies from 40% to 70%.

locations.name: Heavy Minerals (Beach Sand)
locations.summary: Coastal sand deposits between Rushikulya mouth and Gopalpur, containing ilmenite, garnet, and monazite.

keyDeposits: Rushikulya mouth to Gopalpur coastal belt
details.characteristics: Ilmenite, garnet, monazite in coastal sands.
details.uses: Gopalpur port handles export of ilmenite.

locations.name: China Clay
locations.summary: Kaolinitic clay used in ceramics, paper, and refractories.

locations.name: Fire Clay
locations.summary: Leading Indian producer. Recovered alongside coal in Talcher and Ib river coalfields.

locations.name: Pyrophyllite
locations.summary: Industrial mineral used in ceramics, paints, and refractories.

locations.name: Diamonds
locations.summary: Recovered from the gravel beds of the Mahanadi — historically at Hirakud River Island. Newer resources reported in Nuapada.

locations.name: Gemstones
locations.summary: Found in the Granulite belts of the Eastern Ghats. Odisha produces emeralds, rubies, sapphires, and aquamarine.
